blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — carbamazepine hematologic monitoring
stem: A client is starting carbamazepine. Why is pretreatment hematologic testing obtained and why should declining white blood cells or platelets during therapy be followed closely?

options.A: Carbamazepine can cause clinically important bone-marrow suppression, including rare aplastic anemia or agranulocytosis, so baseline counts and meaningful declines require close evaluation.
options.B: Carbamazepine commonly raises white blood cells and platelets as part of its therapeutic effect, so falling counts mainly indicate that seizure control is improving.
options.C: Blood-cell changes are not clinically related to carbamazepine exposure, making baseline testing and follow-up of declining leukocyte or platelet counts unnecessary.
options.D: Any small decrease in a blood-cell count establishes aplastic anemia and requires automatic discontinuation, even when there is no evidence of significant marrow depression.

rationale: The current TEGRETOL label reports aplastic anemia and agranulocytosis and directs complete pretreatment hematologic testing as a baseline. If white blood cell or platelet counts become low or decrease during therapy, close monitoring is required; discontinuation should be considered when significant bone-marrow depression develops. The label also states that most minor hematologic changes do not progress to aplastic anemia or agranulocytosis. Therefore A is correct.
educational_objective: Obtain baseline hematologic testing before carbamazepine and closely evaluate declining white blood cell or platelet counts because clinically significant bone-marrow suppression can occur.
source_locator: Boxed Warning—Aplastic Anemia and Agranulocytosis: obtain complete pretreatment hematologic testing; monitor low/decreased WBC or platelets closely; consider discontinuation if significant bone-marrow depression develops; most minor changes do not progress to aplastic anemia/agranulocytosis.
source_claim_supported: Carbamazepine requires baseline hematologic testing and close follow-up of declining WBC or platelet counts because serious bone-marrow suppression is a recognized risk.
blueprint_locator: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies: monitor medication-related laboratory values and recognize serious adverse effects.
candidate_reasons_resolved: Rewrote all options as full interpretations of hematologic monitoring and balanced their length.
audit_note: Independent adversarial review confirms A uniquely matches the July 2026 TEGRETOL label; no second answer or residual length cue remains.
